page.title: GameForgeJS — Your game. Your code. JavaScript.
hero.intro: From your first character to worlds of your own. A framework for browser games, with classes, components and control over what you build.
hero.node: Node.js is an optional development tool.
demos.title: Code comes to life.
demos.description: Playable examples of movement, combat, cameras, rendering and game rules. The demos are experimental.
demos.platformer: Combos, hitboxes, inventory, skills and manifest-authored levels.
demos.sky: Four expeditions, a gamepad-ready 3D menu, checkpoints and moving platforms.
demos.toon: A Toon ABS sandbox with two large lakes, linked warp gates, five sentries and shallow-water interaction.
demos.note: The demos are small experimental games. Complete courses and upcoming goals are described below.
architecture.title: The framework handles
architecture.description: Levels organize scenes. Entities receive behaviors. Screens and renderers handle presentation. Evolve your game with the classes you already use.
architecture.example: A modular runtime example. The template configures the import map and provides the first level.
progress.intro: Modules organize distribution and extensions. The primary path remains
progress.select: Select runtime groups and addons in
progress.dependencies: . The build includes group dependencies while preserving your game structure.
progress.addons: Parallax, state machines and platformer movement extracted from the demos. Classes built on the framework services and its existing engine.
progress.complete: From zero to a complete game.
progress.goal: Checkpoints already cover action combat, animated models and shallow water. The goal remains a complete Toon adventure and a 2D platformer with at least 20 levels and varied enemy behaviors.
progress.course: Zero to Hero is still in progress. Games, code, assets, lessons and validation will be completed together.
start.intro: Start with a template, choose the modules you need and build your game step by step. The demos above use that same runtime.

page.description: GameForgeJS: an experimental native JavaScript framework for 2D and 3D browser games. Play demos, explore the architecture and follow its progress.
example.toon-adventure-3d: A Toon ABS sandbox with two large lakes, linked warp gates, five sentries and shallow-water interaction.
example.platformer-2d: Two compact stages demonstrating tile collision, jump buffering, coyote time, collection and level transitions.
example.movement-collision-2d: A compact 2D example for movement, collision, and collection.
example.component-adventure-2d: Top-down movement, reusable entity components, and room camera transitions.
example.platform-adventure-2d: Platform combat, patrol and pursuit AI, line of sight, inventory, skills and manifest-authored stages.
example.tactical-rpg-2d: A turn-based grid game with pathfinding, movement range, and combat.
example.fighting-2d: Energy spheres, meter-powered supers, buffered combos, reactive CPU and local versus with four characters.
example.puzzle-battle-2d: An arcade puzzle game with combos and competitive block exchanges.
example.renderer-3d: A rain-soaked basin with planar reflections, wet surfaces, and interactive lighting.
example.solar-system-3d: Procedural celestial materials, sunlight, and animated planetary orbits.
example.sky-trail-3d: Four expeditions, a gamepad-ready 3D menu, moving platforms, checkpoints and collectibles.
example.online-sandbox-2d: Cooperative mining/building, dedicated server rooms, predicted movement and mobile controls; backend required.
example.addons-2d: Shared parallax layers and a patrol/rest state machine using the standard framework lifecycle.
example.touch-garden-2d: Mobile building blocks: identified multi-touch, a virtual stick, a simultaneous dash action, collision and collectible entities.
example.storm-foundry-2d: Layered rain, reactive water reflections, dynamic props, bounded particles and a live FX playground.
a11y.foundry: Open the Storm Foundry FX lab
image.foundry: Storm Foundry: layered rain, water reflections and reactive props rendered by GameForgeJS.
example.aether-observatory-3d: Native WebGL floating islands, shaded architecture, fog, physics traversal, orbit/chase cameras and a skippable cinematic.
example.cinematic-crossing-2d: Parallel camera, zoom and fade tracks, waypoint movement, dialogue cues and clean skip/replay control states.
example.route-atlas-2d: A branching overworld graph, smooth node travel, playable shard trials and event-driven stage unlocks.
example.boss-patterns-2d: A three-phase boss with aimed fans, rings, marked charges, delayed hazards, pooled projectiles and dash invulnerability.
image.aether: Native 3D floating islands, observatory architecture and atmospheric fog
